items.title: This Pyramid Could Be Your Next Intern
items.summary:
Your next intern might be a tiny pyramid-shaped computer 🤖

The Autonomous Intern 2 is built specifically to run AI agents.

You can connect it to Slack, Telegram, or Discord, give it tasks just by talking to it, and keep things like its memory, project files, writing style, and API keys stored locally on the device.

It comes preloaded with OpenClaw or Hermes, and there’s even a Developer Edition where you can run tools like Claude Code, Codex, or your own agent framework.

I’m a sucker for weird AI hardware, and I genuinely love the design of this thing. It starts at $249, and is available to order now through Autonomous's website (no sponsored!)

items.title: Claude’s Text Watermark Could Follow It Everywhere
items.summary:
Anthropic is working on a watermark for Claude-generated text that could follow the text even after you copy, paste, or edit it 👀

They haven't revealed exactly how this watermark works yet, but one way could be by creating a statistical pattern in Claude's word choices that humans can’t see, but a detector potentially could.

And the implications of this have taken the internet by storm. 


People are wondering what happens if Claude only edits something that you originally wrote? Does that now get flagged as AI-generated? What about code, copyright, privacy, or people simply rewriting the text enough to remove the watermark entirely?

And then there’s the bigger debate: Do people have a right to know when something was created with AI? 


Curious where you land on this one. Let me know in the comments 👇

And follow for more AI news and updates.

#AI #ainews #anthropic #claude

items.title: Are AI Models Escaping On Purpose?
items.summary:
Apparently the newest benchmark for AI models is… can it commit cyber crimes? 😭

First OpenAI’s model broke out during testing and hacked Hugging Face.

Then Anthropic basically showed up like, “our models commit crimes too.”

And now Meta has joined the club after one of its AI models accidentally got access to the public internet during cybersecurity testing and started hacking another company.

Obviously, there are some very real and slightly terrifying implications here about what happens when increasingly capable AI systems get access to tools they weren’t supposed to have.

But I also can’t get over how these stories are starting to feel like a very weird flex from the AI companies like: "Our model is so smart it broke containment too!”

Follow to stay up-to-date with what's happening in the tech and AI world!

#ainews #ai #meta #openai #anthropic
